strengths: Novel application of bilevel optimization to jointly model SSL pre-training and downstream fine-tuning, first of its kind in this formulation
Rigorous mathematical framework with sound implicit gradient derivation following the implicit function theorem
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 14 diverse downstream datasets with proper uncertainty quantification (10 random seeds, reported means/std)
Valuable feature visualizations (t-SNE) showing improved feature alignment even on datasets without accuracy gains
Demonstrated robustness of improvements across varying pre-training durations (Figure 2), suggesting efficiency gains beyond just more training
Clear presentation with helpful pipeline diagrams and mathematical notation
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scale: only ResNet-18 on STL10 pre-training; raises critical questions about generalizability to modern large-scale SSL scenarios
Marginal and inconsistent improvements: most gains are 0.1-0.3% with 4/14 datasets showing regression; no statistical significance testing despite overlapping error bars
Unquantified computational overhead: acknowledged significant cost from CG approximation but no wall-clock time or FLOP analysis provided, undermining cost-benefit analysis
Theory-practice mismatch: implicit gradient derivation assumes φP is fixed (A.1) but Algorithm 1 updates φP at every iteration; stationary condition assumed but never enforced
Insufficient ablation studies: multiple critical hyperparameters (λ=0.001, γ=0.01, α=0.1, Na=100) lack justification; no sensitivity analysis despite complex interactions
Missing comparisons with related methods: COIN, Noisy-Tune, Spin, RIFLE mentioned as related priming techniques but none compared against; only baseline is conventional SSL
Questionable experimental design: additional downstream head warm-up stage in BiSSL pipeline not in baseline makes direct comparison problematic
Limited analysis of results: no investigation of which task types benefit from BiSSL, no explanation of failures (regressions on STL10L, CIFAR100), ad-hoc design choices (γ term for 'stability')

strengths: Interesting novel application of bilevel optimization to align pretext pre-training and downstream fine-tuning stages in SSL
Solid theoretical framework with detailed implicit gradient derivations and analysis of how λ controls the pre-training vs downstream trade-off
Comprehensive evaluation across 14 diverse downstream datasets (fine-grained recognition, scene understanding, texture analysis)
Improvements demonstrated on 10/14 datasets with no significant regressions
Reproducibility efforts including detailed hyperparameter tables, promised code release, and thorough appendices
Qualitative feature analysis via t-SNE visualizations provides intuitive support for improved feature alignment
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scope: only ResNet-18 on STL10 (100k images); no large-scale validation on ImageNet or with larger models, limiting generalizability
Empirical improvements are modest and lack statistical validation—many gains fall within standard deviation (e.g., Cars +0.3%, Aircraft +0.8%), some show regressions (STL10L -0.1%, CIFAR100 -0.2%)
Critical practical limitation: computational overhead from conjugate gradient approximations not quantified—no wall-clock time, memory, or FLOPs comparisons provided despite acknowledged overhead
Theory-practice gap: Algorithm 1 runs lower-level for only 20 steps but theory assumes convergence to stationary point (θ*_P(θD) ∈ argmin); this fundamental violation of assumptions is unaddressed

Methodological fairness concerns: different hyperparameter configurations for baseline vs BiSSL (Tables 2-4), different pretext training schedules (600 vs 500+~100 epochs), extensive grid search (200 configs) susceptible to overfitting

Questionable design choices without justification: γ term added purely for 'empirical stability' suggesting unstable core formulation; λ=0.001 from 'early experiments' with no ablations; CG iterations=5 appears arbitrary
Missing ablation studies on critical hyperparameters (λ, γ, α) and regularization form r(·,·), making it unclear which components drive any improvements
Limited novelty: straightforward application of existing BLO techniques (implicit gradients, CG) to new domain; coupling via simple L2 regularization lacks sophisticated design
Unverified theoretical assumptions: claims about convexity due to λ lack formal proof; Hessian invertibility not verified for CNNs; ϕP fixed in derivations but actually optimized in practice
Incomplete feature analysis: t-SNE visualizations are subjective and can mislead; improvements sometimes marginal; no quantitative clustering metrics (silhouette score, purity)

strengths: Novel application of bilevel optimization: First framework to jointly model pre-training and fine-tuning as interdependent BLO levels, addressing a well-motivated problem of distribution misalignment in SSL
Mathematically sound theoretical framework: Clear bilevel formulation with proper implicit gradient derivation following established techniques and correctly stated assumptions

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: 14 diverse downstream datasets with proper experimental protocol (10 runs, mean/std reporting, 200-config hyperparameter search), showing consistent improvements on 10/14 datasets
Insightful qualitative analysis: t-SNE visualizations convincingly demonstrate improved downstream feature alignment, validating the core hypothesis even where accuracy gains are marginal
Robustness validation: Figure 2 shows improvements persist across different pre-training epochs, suggesting benefits from improved information transfer rather than just additional training
Strong reproducibility support: Detailed implementation appendix, extensive hyperparameter tables, clear algorithms, and promised code/weight release facilitate reproduction
Clear presentation: Well-motivated writing, comprehensive derivations, effective visualizations, and logical flow make the work accessible
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scale: Only ResNet-18 on STL10 due to resource constraints; no experiments on larger models (ResNet-50+, Vision Transformers) or modern SSL methods, making generalizability to current practice unclear

Incomplete theoretical justification: (1) ϕP fixed assumption acknowledged but never removed, (2) stationary condition required for Eq. 6 assumed but not verified during training, (3) convexity claim for G stated without proof, (4) no convergence guarantees

Insufficient ablation studies: Critical hyperparameters (λ=0.001, γ=0.01, α=0.1, Na=100) appear arbitrary with minimal justification; no systematic ablation on γ (direct downstream loss weighting) which seems fundamental

Missing comparisons with related work: No experimental comparison with mentioned priming methods (COIN, Noisy-Tune, RIFLE, Spin) or alternative BLO formulations, limiting assessment of BiSSL's relative merit

Modest improvements on key benchmarks: Negligible gain on STL10L itself (-0.1%), ~0.1-0.9% on CIFAR/standard datasets (within error bars), largest gains only on smaller specialized datasets; practical significance questionable
Computational cost not quantified: No wall-clock time comparisons despite CG iterations and multi-stage pipeline adding overhead; practical utility assessment incomplete
Ad-hoc design choices: γ term justified only as 'empirically improving stability' without principled explanation; upper-level backbone adaptation via EMA (α=0.1) lacks justification
Pipeline complexity burden: Requires 4 sequential training stages with separate hyperparameters per stage, multiplying tuning burden vs. standard SSL→fine-tune approach
Limited analysis of when BiSSL helps: Improvements vary widely (-0.2% to +2.8%) across datasets with no characterization of which dataset properties benefit from BiSSL

strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation: clearly articulates distribution misalignment between pretext and downstream data and proposes a principled bilevel optimization solution
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 12 downstream datasets, 2 pretext methods, 10 random seeds per configuration, 100 hyperparameter configurations per dataset
Rigorous mathematical development: proper implicit gradient derivations with explicit expressions, clear articulation of assumptions, and intuitive interpretation of regularization parameter λ
Task-agnostic framework applicable across different pretext/downstream combinations without specialization to specific choices
Supporting visual evidence: t-SNE visualizations effectively demonstrate improved feature alignment for downstream tasks, even on datasets without accuracy gains
Thorough documentation: extensive implementation details in appendices support reproducibility
weaknesses: Modest and inconsistent improvements lacking statistical rigor: many gains are marginal (e.g., +0.3% CIFAR10, +0.5% CIFAR100), some datasets show no improvement, and crucially, no significance testing despite overlapping error bars in several cases

Computational overhead inadequately analyzed: conjugate gradient requires multiple Hessian-vector products but no wall-clock time comparisons provided; 'negligible' 8-epoch claim lacks empirical support
Weak theoretical justification: the connection between the bilevel formulation and improved downstream alignment is indirect; why this specific formulation is optimal is not deeply explained

Ad-hoc implementation complexity: multi-stage pipeline (SSL→head warm-up→BiSSL→fine-tuning) with multiple hyperparameters (λ=0.001, T=500, N_U/N_L) chosen from 'early experiments'; subjective hyperparameter selection contradicts reproducibility
Critical missing ablations: no ablation studies on regularization weight λ, number of alternations T, iteration counts N_U/N_L, or alternative regularization functions r; limited sensitivity analysis
Dependency on pre-training quality: Figure 2 shows benefits only after ~300 epochs of pre-training, raising unclear mechanism questions and limiting applicability when pre-training is already strong
Limited experimental scope: only ResNet-50 backbone and image classification (+single object detection dataset); no Vision Transformers, other architectures, or non-vision modalities
Incomplete related work comparison: mentions COIN, Noisy-Tune, Spin, RIFLE methods but provides no empirical comparison on identical datasets
Theoretical assumptions mismatched to practice: implicit gradient derivation assumes fixed φ_P contradicting joint optimization; Hessian invertibility assumed but not verified
Reproducibility concerns: subjective design choices, complex multi-stage pipeline, and unverified code release claim may hinder exact reproduction

strengths: Well-articulated motivation identifying a real limitation of standard SSL pipelines
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 12 datasets, two pretext tasks, and object detection with proper statistical reporting
Mathematically sound implicit gradient derivation with clear interpretation of the scaling parameter λ
Consistent improvements across most datasets (10-11/12) with lower or comparable variance to baseline
Detailed hyperparameter documentation and promised code release support reproducibility
Visual inspection of learned representations via t-SNE visualizations provides qualitative insights
weaknesses: Limited novelty: applies existing BLO techniques to a known problem; similar ideas already addressed by COIN, Noisy-Tune, Spin, RIFLE, and other concurrent BLO works in SSL
Modest empirical improvements often within statistical noise (e.g., +0.3% ± 0.2%, 0.0% ± 0.1%); largest gains on niche datasets only

Insufficient computational cost analysis: method requires expensive Hessian-vector products via CG but provides no wall-clock time comparisons; practical utility questionable given computational overhead

Significant theory-practice gaps: (1) implicit gradient assumes fixed ϕ_P but algorithm updates ϕ_P; (2) stationary condition is fragile, requiring careful initialization rather than random initialization, undermining theoretical generality; (3) regularization-induced convexity feels artificial
Critical missing ablations on key hyperparameters (λ, N_U, N_L, T) and no ablation on the second term in Eq. 2, claimed to be 'not strictly necessary' but 'empirically helpful'

No experimental comparison with existing alignment methods (COIN, Noisy-Tune, Spin, RIFLE), making it impossible to assess if BiSSL offers genuine advantages or is merely one of several reasonable approaches
Unfair experimental design in Figure 2: BiSSL receives additional computational budget (~100 expensive Hessian iterations) compared to fair fixed-budget comparison
Missing analysis of failure cases and dataset properties determining effectiveness; no quantitative metrics (e.g., silhouette score) for clustering quality claims
T-SNE visualizations show qualitative improvements but don't rigorously establish causal connection between feature clustering and downstream fine-tuning performance
Limited scope of distribution shift scenarios: all downstream datasets are natural images with mild shift from ImageNet; unclear generalization to extreme distribution mismatch

strengths: Novel problem formulation: Treating SSL pre-training and downstream fine-tuning as a bilevel optimization problem is intuitive, well-motivated, and represents a fresh perspective on the SSL pipeline

Comprehensive experimental validation: Evaluation on 12 downstream classification datasets, object detection, variable pre-training durations, and two pretext tasks (SimCLR/BYOL) demonstrates thoroughness
Consistent empirical improvements: 10/12 datasets show performance gains with no degradation; substantial improvements on several datasets (CUB200 +9.6%, Pets +6.4%)
Technical soundness: Mathematically rigorous bilevel formulation with clear implicit gradient derivations; proper assumptions stated and development is rigorous
Task-agnostic framework: Algorithm works with different pretext and downstream tasks without modification, showing practical generality
Strong presentation and reproducibility: Well-organized paper with detailed appendices, extensive implementation details (Tables 3-5), and promised code release facilitates reproduction
Supporting evidence for alignment: Feature visualizations and stable results across runs support the core hypothesis that BiSSL improves downstream task alignment
weaknesses: Insufficient analysis of computational overhead: Conjugate gradient approximation of inverse Hessian-vector products introduces non-trivial computational cost (Nc=5 CG iterations per upper-level step), but no wall-clock time comparisons or efficiency analysis provided; this is acknowledged but deferred to future work

Critical missing comparisons: No experimental comparison with directly related 'priming' methods (COIN, Noisy-Tune, Spin, RIFLE) mentioned in Section 2—these are the most relevant baselines for bridging pre-training and fine-tuning and their absence is a notable gap

Key design choices lack ablation studies: (1) The second term L^D(θD, φD) in Eq. (2) is stated to improve stability 'empirically' without evidence or ablation; (2) Regularization weight λ=0.001 chosen from 'early experiments' without sensitivity analysis; (3) No ablations on regularization form, CG parameters, or alternation scheme

Limited analysis of when/why BiSSL helps: Improvements vary widely across datasets (CUB200 +9.6% vs Cars 0.0%), but no characterization of which dataset/task properties determine effectiveness; the analysis in Section 4.3.2 is somewhat superficial

Reduced novelty in methodology: Several prior works apply BLO to SSL (Gupta et al. 2022, LoGo, OSSL, MetaMask, BLO-SAM); the implicit gradient derivation closely follows Rajeswaran et al. (2019); novelty is primarily in problem formulation rather than algorithmic innovation

Initialization dependencies and assumptions: Requires careful staged initialization (pretext → head warm-up → BiSSL), reducing practical novelty; stationary condition assumptions may not hold robustly during SGD training; convexity and Hessian invertibility assumptions may be violated in practice

Hyperparameter complexity and generalization concerns: Multiple new hyperparameters (λ, NL, NU, T, CG settings); different per-dataset configurations (Tables 3-5) raise generalization questions; downstream head warm-up uses 'adjusted' hyperparameters (vague); extensive grid search (100 configs) may not reflect practical deployability

Qualitative feature analysis: t-SNE visualizations lack proper parameter specification and quantitative clustering metrics; t-SNE is known to be sensitive and can be misleading; silhouette scores or Davies-Bouldin indices would strengthen claims
Limited object detection validation: Only one detection benchmark (VOC07+12); modest improvements (+1.0-2.1%); broader detection task validation would increase confidence in generality

Modest improvements on many datasets: While consistent, many improvements are 0.1-0.5%; practical significance given added complexity is unclear; no statistical significance testing (e.g., t-tests) provided
